artboards.title: Option B · Under the Hood — interactive

annotations.text:
HOW WAYPOINT WORKS — three directions for a single screen that shows a family the process loop, a bit of how to use the app, and a bit of what's happening under the hood.

This is a NEW product-tour screen, separate from the existing "How the System Works" process map (which explains the Regional Center / IPP process, not the app itself).

All three keep the same four loop stages so they're a fair comparison: TELL (you describe your situation) → PLAN (Waypoint gives one next step, checked against CA law) → ACT (a friendly, drafted ask) → TRACK (Waypoint runs the clock, firms up tone if it has to) → loops back to TELL/PLAN as things change. Built from waypoint-app/src/lib/theme.ts's warm brand tokens and the real Brandmark (pin + route line).

STATUS (Sep 12): owner is leaning toward A and B. Both are now real interactive prototypes (is_interactive) — tap through them on the canvas, not just look. C stays as a static reference; Main still mirrors it pending a final pick.

OPTION A · THE LOOP — now interactive

A literal circular cycle diagram — four stage nodes ringed around a center hub, with a detail card below that updates to the tapped stage.

How it interacts: tap any of the 4 nodes to select that stage (it fills pine, the detail card below updates); tap the center hub to advance to the NEXT stage in sequence, demonstrating the loop actually turning; tap "UNDER THE HOOD" to collapse/expand that panel.

Motivation: most direct answer to "show me the loop" — the shape does the explaining before you read a word.
Tradeoff: the most implementation surface of the three if built as a real component (absolute-positioned ring math, not a simple list).

OPTION B · UNDER THE HOOD — now interactive

A cutaway: a top strip you do (Tell → Plan → Act → Track) sits over a dark "engine" panel showing what Waypoint is doing for each one.

How it interacts: tap a top chip OR its matching engine row — either highlights both, visually proving the cutaway's central claim (this visible step causes that hidden mechanism); tap the dashed "UNDER THE HOOD" seam to collapse/expand the whole engine panel.

Motivation: most literal answer to "what's happening under the hood" — the mechanism is the centerpiece, and now the link between action and mechanism is provable by tapping, not just implied by position.
Tradeoff: says less about the loop itself (repeat is one line, not a diagram) — leads with the AI's work over the family's.

OPTION C · THE ROUTE — recommended starting point

A winding route with four numbered waypoint pins, using the app's own pin-and-route mark (never a compass, per Brandmark.astro) — the loop is a round trip back to pin 1.

Motivation: the only option that IS the brand ("a GPS for the disability services journey") rather than illustrating it generically; lightest under-the-hood treatment keeps it from feeling technical.
Tradeoff: the map reads best once — a returning user may want A's or B's denser recap faster than re-walking a route.
